findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new `unsubscribe` action calls `slugs_do_not_match`, a method that does not exist — the controller's slug-mismatch helper is defined with a trailing question mark as `slugs_do_not_match?` (the same guard `show` uses). Every request to the emailed link /t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe raises NoMethodError (undefined method `slugs_do_not_match`) before the redirect or the toggle runs, returning a 500 — the feature's only server endpoint is dead on arrival for every recipient.

[BUG] `unsubscribe_url` builds on `url` (`"#{url}/unsubscribe"`), which returns a site-relative path like /t/<slug>/<id> — the same email template in this diff proves it by concatenating `Discourse.base_url` with `post.url` — so the new method omits the host. The mailer passes this value into the email footer's %{unsubscribe_url}, so every notification email contains a hostless link (/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe) that mail clients cannot resolve; unlike the adjacent user_preferences_url, which message_builder explicitly builds as "#{Discourse.base_url}/my/preferences", the 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' link is unclickable for every recipient.

[BUG] The model hook invokes `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, a method the post-stream model does not define and that this diff adds nowhere. Booting the client on the unsubscribe URL throws `PostStream.loadTopicView is not a function`, the model hook rejects, and the unsubscribe screen never renders — the controller, view, template, and SCSS added in this diff become unreachable dead code.

[BUG] The template is created at the nested-route path `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, but the route map registers the top-level route `topicUnsubscribe` (whose route/controller/view files this same diff places under the dashed names `topic-unsubscribe`), and the resolver looks up its template as the dashed module `discourse/templates/topic-unsubscribe` — the slashed directory form is only produced from dotted nested names like `topic.unsubscribe`. The template module is never resolved for the top-level route, so the page renders blank (no stop-notifications text, no topic-notifications-button) even for a logged-in user who reaches the URL.

[BUG] `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is immediately dereferenced as `tu.notification_level` with no nil guard, but no topic_users row exists for a logged-in user who has never opened that topic. Any logged-in user hitting an unsubscribe URL for a topic they have no topic_users row for (e.g., clicking a forwarded link from a different account, or any guessed topic URL) gets `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil` and a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page.

[ADVISORY] The action mutates notification_level on a plain GET with no CSRF token, no confirmation step, and no write-protection on the slugless variant. Any third-party page can silently demute or remute any topic for every logged-in user via an embedded `` (Rails request-forgery protection does not cover GET), and mail-client link prefetchers trigger the same state change without the user ever seeing a page.

[ADVISORY] The action mutates `tu` directly and calls `tu.save!`, bypassing `TopicUser.change`, the sanctioned write path that publishes the `notification_level_change` MessageBus message for /topic/<id>. A user with the topic open in another tab sees a stale watching/tracking state (topic header button, browser tab title updates) until reload, because the MessageBus channel never receives the change this action made — every other notification-level write in the same model file publishes it.

[ADVISORY] The toggle demotes tracking/watching users only to `regular` rather than to `muted`, while regular-level users still receive direct-reply and mention notifications for the topic. A watching user who clicks the emailed 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' link continues to receive reply/mention emails for that topic — the email's promise is only kept after a second visit fully mutes them, and users will report the unsubscribe as broken.

[ADVISORY] No spec anywhere in the diff exercises the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (slug-mismatch redirect, slugless redirect, notification toggle, render path) or the new client route; the only test change tweaks the message_builder spec to hardcode a relative `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, codifying the missing base_url. The NameError that 500s every unsubscribe request and the nil-TopicUser crash both ship undetected — a minimal request spec per branch of the action would have caught both before merge, and the mailer spec as written can never catch a hostless unsubscribe link.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by without a nil guard, so any logged-in user without a pre-existing TopicUser row for the topic raises NoMethodError on nil.notification_level. A forum member opening a forwarded unsubscribe link (or any logged-in user constructing /t/<id>/unsubscribe for a topic they have never visited or been emailed about) gets a 500 error page; the action also cannot unsubscribe such users at all because it neither creates the row nor falls back to TopicUser.change's find_or_create.

[BUG] The level transition demotes tracking/watching users to :regular instead of :muted, contradicting the acceptance criteria stated by this PR's own copy — server.en.yml unsubscribe_link promises "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here" and client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications renders "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}" on the confirmation page. A watching or tracking user who clicks unsubscribe lands at :regular and still receives direct reply/mention/quote notification emails for that topic, so the link appears broken to exactly the users most likely to click it (post notifications); only a second click, once at :regular, reaches :muted and actually stops the mail.

[ADVISORY] The action hand-rolls the notification-level mutation (find_by + assignment + save!) instead of using the canonical TopicUser.change API, which in this same diff (app/models/topic_user.rb:110-112) publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change event on every level change. The user's other open sessions never receive the /topic/<id> notification_level_change MessageBus message, so an open tab keeps showing the stale Watching/Tracking state, and the codebase now has two parallel mutation paths for notification_level that will drift the next time change() gains a side effect.

[ADVISORY] The entire feature ships with zero behavioral test coverage: the only test change in the diff adds unsubscribe_url to an existing message_builder fixture so a pre-existing List-Unsubscribe header assertion stays green, and no spec exercises the new behavior — the topics#unsubscribe level-transition branch, the slug redirect, the missing-TopicUser case, Topic#unsubscribe_url, or the assertion that a rendered notification email actually contains the per-topic link. A regression in the transition logic (flipping the > comparison, or swapping :regular and :muted) silently changes users' notification levels and keeps CI green; the PR's headline acceptance criterion — the unsubscribe link present and resolvable in notification emails — has no automated check, so a future message_builder or locale refactor can drop or break the link undetected.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe mutates TopicUser.notification_level on a plain GET with no authenticity token, no per-user token in the emailed URL, and no confirmation step — the mutation fires on page load before the user makes any choice on the rendered page. Any logged-in Discourse user who merely loads the URL gets their notification level silently toggled: an attacker can embed on any third-party page and mute (or repeatedly toggle) every logged-in victim who views it, muting victims out of topics without their knowledge; re-clicking an old email also toggles the level to a different state each time.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by returns nil for any logged-in user without a TopicUser row for the topic, and tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError on nil. Any logged-in user who opens a forwarded unsubscribe link (or hand-visits /t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe) for a topic they have never interacted with receives a 500 error instead of an unsubscribe flow — the code assumes the email recipient's TopicUser row always exists and never creates it or 4xx's.

[BUG] The unsubscribe toggle clamps any level above regular down to regular instead of muted, so one click on the email link does not unsubscribe the very users who receive topic notification emails. A watching or tracking user who clicks the email's 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' link lands at regular, still receives replied/mentioned/quoted notification emails for that topic, and the landing page falsely asserts 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>' — the feature's core promise is unfulfilled for its primary audience, who must discover the dropdown and click a second time.

[BUG] The shared unsubscribe_link locale now requires a %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation value, but Email::MessageBuilder builds @template_args from only site_name/base_url/user_preferences_url plus caller opts and never defaults unsubscribe_url, and the diff supplies it from exactly one call site (UserNotifications#send_notification_email). Every other add_unsubscribe_link: true caller — plugin mailers and any in-tree mailer not touched by this diff — raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the email is built (line 68's I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)) and those emails silently stop delivering; the diff's own message_builder_spec had to add unsubscribe_url to keep passing, proving the key is now mandatory while only one side of the writer/reader pair was migrated.

[ADVISORY] The new state-changing topics#unsubscribe action (login gating, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, level-toggle semantics, save, show rendering) ships with zero tests — the only spec the diff touches is message_builder_spec. The toggle semantics (watching→regular rather than muted) and the nil-TopicUser path have no regression net, so these defects ship green and any future change to notification_levels semantics breaks the email-unsubscribe contract with no failing build.

[ADVISORY] The PR rewrites the entire core topic-loading route (var→const, declaration reshuffling into the const list, blank-line churn) with no behavioral need traceable to the unsubscribe feature. A mechanical rewrite of the route that serves every topic navigation inflates the feature diff, guarantees merge conflicts with in-flight branches, and buries any accidental semantic change in a file reviewers are diffing for an unrelated feature; the rewrite itself carries regression risk with no covering test.

[ADVISORY] The diff carries five zero-behavior hunks in a core model — re-indentation of the tracking scope args (10-12), the create_lookup rewrite (59-65), and three one-liner conversions of MessageBus.publish/where/update_all calls (113, 125, 194, 218) — none traceable to the unsubscribe requirement. Pure formatting churn in TopicUser turns the feature review into noise and guarantees conflicts for parallel branches; a regression hidden inside the tracking-scope re-indentation ships invisible next to the real change, and blame/bisect for the feature is polluted.

[ADVISORY] The respond_instructions assignment is rewritten from if/else to a trailing conditional if-expression purely for style, interleaved with the single functional delta of this PR. Unrelated reformatting inside the email-builder hot path makes the functional line (the one that matters for this feature) harder to spot in review and forces every in-flight branch touching message_builder to re-resolve conflicts with no requirement gained.

[ADVISORY] The from_alias guard is converted to a one-line conditional modifier with no functional change, unrelated to the unsubscribe_url line added two hunks up in the same method. Style-only churn in the central notification-mailer method inflates the diff reviewers must scan for the actual feature change and creates spurious merge conflicts for parallel mailer work.

[ADVISORY] The entire notification email template is re-indented and restructured with zero functional delta — respond_instructions still renders twice when context_posts is present, before and after — as churn unrelated to the feature. A 100%-rewritten email template means anyone bisecting an email rendering regression after this PR must wade through a whole-file diff to discover only whitespace changed, and the restructure guarantees conflicts with any parallel template work.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled stopNotificiationsText and the same misspelling is mirrored in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs line 3, so the two files must keep the wrong token in lockstep. Anyone correcting the spelling on one side only (the natural cleanup) silently blanks the unsubscribe page body — triple-stache over a missing property renders empty with no Ember error — and no one searching the codebase for 'stopNotificationsText' finds the property.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe does `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` with no nil guard, but a logged-in recipient of the notification email need not have a TopicUser row (mentioned/quoted users and category-watchers receive these emails without ever having opened the topic), so the lookup returns nil and the action raises NoMethodError. The unsubscribe link 500s for exactly the class of user most likely to click it; the codebase's canonical upsert API `TopicUser.change(user.id, topic_id, ...)` — which the very mailer embedding this link calls in user_notifications.rb for last_emailed_post_number — handles the row-missing case and is bypassed by this hand-rolled find/mutate path.

[BUG] The new guard calls `slugs_do_not_match`, but the controller's predicate used for the identical branch in `show` is `slugs_do_not_match?` (with the question mark), so the action raises NoMethodError on undefined method `slugs_do_not_match` before reaching any other line of the action. Every GET of /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe — the URL this diff stamps into every notification email — returns a 500, making the whole feature dead on arrival; both the redirect branch and the mutation branch sit behind this call, so no code path survives.

[BUG] The new `topicUnsubscribe` route at `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` is declared after the existing `topic.fromParamsNear` route at `/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost` (visible two lines above in the same file), and Ember's router recognizes the earlier-declared route first, so the unsubscribe URL binds nearPost="unsubscribe" to the plain topic route and `topicUnsubscribe` never activates. The unsubscribe confirmation page (route, controller, view, and template — all four new client files) is unreachable dead code; users clicking the email link land on the ordinary topic view with the garbage nearPost flowing into the setupController whose own comment says "closest post is null and this is exploding", and they get no feedback that their notification level was changed.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe performs a persistent state change (`tu.save!`) on a plain GET with no token, no confirmation, and no guard on the transition, making it the only mutation endpoint in the controller reachable via a side-effecting unauthenticated-token GET. Any third-party page can embed `` — the slug-mismatch branch even 301-redirects to the canonical URL and re-fires — and silently flip the logged-in viewer's notification level (watching→regular, regular→muted) while they never leave the attacker's page.

[BUG] The toggle demotes tracking/watching users only to :regular instead of :muted, and regular still emails the user replies, mentions, and quotes for that topic, so the action does not do what the same diff's email copy categorically promises ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic"). A watcher who clicks unsubscribe keeps receiving notification emails for the topic and concludes the unsubscribe is broken (spam complaints follow); they must click the link twice — watching→regular→muted — to get the behavior the email promised in one click.

[ADVISORY] The action mutates notification_level via direct find/assign/save! instead of the canonical `TopicUser.change` API, silently dropping the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", {notification_level_change: ...})` side effect that every other notification_level write path performs (visible in topic_user.rb in this very diff). A user's other open sessions never receive the notification_level_change message, so the topic notification button shows a stale level until reload; and a second hand-maintained mutation path for the same field has already drifted from the first on both upsert and publish semantics, so the next change to notification semantics must be made twice.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten `unsubscribe_link` string introduces a required `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, and Email::MessageBuilder's html_part (message_builder.rb line 67) passes template_args straight into `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, so any mail built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without the new companion `unsubscribe_url` opt now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time. The builder's public option gained a hidden required parameter with no fallback default — the diff's own message_builder_spec had to be patched to pass unsubscribe_url just to keep constructing — so any core mailer or plugin email outside this diff that sets add_unsubscribe_link stops sending and raises during message construction.

[ADVISORY] The new topics#unsubscribe action — carrying a 301-redirect branch, a two-branch notification-level toggle, and a TopicUser lookup — ships with no request spec anywhere in the diff (the only spec touched is the email builder's). The two P1 500s in this action (the predicate-name NoMethodError at line 101 and the nil-TopicUser NoMethodError at line 107) reach production precisely because nothing exercises the route that every notification email now links to; a single anonymous-and-logged-in request spec would have caught both.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError because TopicUser.find_by returns nil whenever the current user has no TopicUser row — exactly the situation for a user who received the notification email via an @mention without ever opening the topic, and for an anonymous (logged-out) click where current_user is already nil. A mention-notified user who never visited the topic (or anyone whose email client opens the link while logged out) clicks the emailed 'stop receiving notifications' link and gets a 500 error page instead of being unsubscribed; the feature is broken end-to-end for this whole class of recipients.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action demotes watching/tracking users only to notification_level :regular instead of muting, so a single click on the emailed 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' link does not stop reply/@mention notification emails — and for a tracking user the change is a notification no-op entirely, since tracking and regular have identical email triggers. A watching/tracking user clicks unsubscribe, is shown the confirmation 'You will stop receiving notifications for {title}' (config/locales/client.en.yml), and then keeps receiving reply and mention emails for that topic; the PR's stated objective (unsubscribe) was silently replaced by a one-notch demotion, producing direct 'unsubscribe doesn't work' complaints.

[BUG] The unsubscribe routes are state-mutating GETs whose action is also a toggle (topics_controller.rb:107-111), so every full reload of the confirmation URL re-executes the mutation and flips a regular-level user to muted, and any automated fetcher of the emailed URL (mail scanner, link-preview prefetcher) triggers the state change with no user click at all. A user who lands on /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe and presses F5 (or whose mail gateway prefetches the link) is silently muted — losing mention and reply notifications for the topic — while the page keeps claiming they merely stopped notifications; the change leaves no trace of being user-initiated.

[ADVISORY] The action hand-rolls the notification-level update (find_by plus assignment plus save!) instead of calling TopicUser.change, and the hand-rolled copy has already drifted from its source of truth within this same diff: it lacks change's create-if-missing upsert (the nil crash above) and drops change's MessageBus.publish of notification_level_change. The user's already-open tab on that topic keeps showing the stale 'Watching' state until reload, and every future change to level-change semantics (upsert, bus events) must now be replicated in two places or silently diverge again — the second copy is where the nil crash was born.

[ADVISORY] The entire new state-mutating TopicsController#unsubscribe action (slug-redirect branch, demote-vs-mute toggle, nil TopicUser path) ships with zero specs — the only test touched in this diff asserts the presence of a List-Unsubscribe mail header. Both blocking defects in this very diff (nil NoMethodError for mention-notified users, demote-to-regular instead of unsubscribe) would have been caught by a basic controller spec, so regressions in the email unsubscribe flow surface only when end users report 500s or continued emails.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled stopNotificiationsText ('Notificiations') and the triple-stache binding in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 must reproduce the typo verbatim for any confirmation text to render. A maintainer who corrects the spelling in either the controller or the template alone silently blanks the unsubscribe page with no error, and anyone searching the codebase for the correctly spelled 'stopNotifications' finds nothing.

[ADVISORY] send_notification_email is the shared builder for private-message notification emails as well, so the new per-topic unsubscribe sentence and link are unconditionally injected into direct-message emails, where clicking it mutes the entire private conversation while the copy presents it as unsubscribing from a 'topic'. A PM recipient who clicks 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' silently stops being notified of all further messages in that private conversation — a materially stronger action than unsubscribing from a public topic's emails — with nothing in the email indicating they are muting a private message thread.

[BUG] The new unsubscribe action mutates the user's topic notification state via `tu.save!` on a plain unauthenticated GET request carrying no CSRF token and no per-user unsubscribe key, while line 32 explicitly skips the check_xhr filter that gates every other mutating action in this controller, making the mutation cross-site forgeable (Rails authenticity tokens never apply to GET, so Discourse's XHR requirement was the only barrier and it is bypassed for this action). Any attacker-controlled web page embeds `` — the slug-less route added at config/routes.rb:440-441 301-redirects to the canonical URL and browsers follow redirects inside img tags automatically, so only the topic id is needed — and every logged-in user whose browser renders the page has that topic silently demoted (watching/tracking to regular, regular to muted), corrupting their notification preferences with no confirmation and no visible feedback until notifications stop arriving.

[BUG] `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil for any logged-in user who has no TopicUser row for the requested topic (a row is only created on first view, watch, or notification email), and line 108 dereferences that nil with `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError. Any logged-in user who opens the unsubscribe URL for any readable topic they have never interacted with gets an unhandled NoMethodError and a 500 response from the endpoint the emails advertise, instead of a settings change or an error page — the crash is trivially reachable with a handcrafted URL for any public topic.

[ADVISORY] The template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` with a triple-stash (unescaped), and that string is built by interpolating the user-controlled topic title (`model.fancyTitle`) into an HTML-bearing I18n message (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 lines 4-6), so topic-title content reaches the DOM with no escaping at the sink. Any markup that survives the server-side title cooking pipeline — or any future loosening of title sanitization or a site translation override — executes as stored XSS in the session of every user who follows the email's unsubscribe link; the page's safety rests entirely on a server-side sanitization step that this template never re-verifies, unlike escaped bindings elsewhere.

[ADVISORY] The email footer added in config/locales/server.en.yml promises 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here', but the action demotes watching/tracking users only to `regular`, a level that still emails direct replies and mentions, so the first click does not actually stop the mail. Users who click the unsubscribe link keep receiving reply/mention notification emails for the topic and conclude the unsubscribe feature is broken — the operator absorbs the spam complaints and support load, and full silence requires a second visit to flip regular to muted.

[BUG] The PR's only test modification (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb is the sole test-shaped file in the diff — I checked all diff paths for spec/test files and found no other) adds unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to the message_with_unsubscribe fixture, but no assertion verifies any of the new per-topic unsubscribe behavior: the assertion consuming the fixture, expect(message_with_unsubscribe.header_args['List-Unsubscribe']).to be_present, checks only that a header key exists and never inspects its value or URL, and the fixture carries no html_override, so Email::MessageBuilder#html_part — the only code path that cooks I18n.t('unsubscribe_link') and substitutes %{unsubscribe_link} (now containing the new %{unsubscribe_url}) into the email body — returns nil immediately and is never executed by this spec. The spec change is inert test theater: the suite passes identically whether the feature works or not, so a regression in Topic#unsubscribe_url (app/models/topic.rb:719-721), in the mailer pass-through unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:295), or in the new %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation in server.en.yml's unsubscribe_link — including an I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument raised at email-render time for any add_unsubscribe_link caller that omits the option — ships green; a broken per-topic unsubscribe link in production emails is caught by no test, while the diff's touching of the spec file creates the false impression that the email-side behavior change is covered. The hardcoded "/t/1234/unsubscribe" fixture also never exercises the URL shape Topic#unsubscribe_url actually produces, so even the value-level correctness of the link is unverified.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by with no nil guard, so any logged-in user without a pre-existing TopicUser row for the topic crashes with NoMethodError (undefined method `notification_level' for nil:NilClass) and gets a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page. The /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe URL is printed in the footer of every post-notification email and is trivially guessable/forwardable; TopicUser rows are created lazily on visit or first notification email and were never backfilled, so any user who clicks a shared or forwarded unsubscribe link for a topic they never visited or tracked hits a hard 500 (email recipients themselves only survive because UserNotifications#send_notification_email creates their row via TopicUser.change).

[BUG] The unsubscribe handler demotes watching/tracking users to regular rather than muted, so the email link's added promise 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' is not delivered — those users keep receiving reply/mention notification emails for the topic after clicking it. A watching or tracking user — the heaviest email recipients this feature targets — clicks the advertised 'stop receiving notifications' link, is set to notification_level regular, and still receives a notification email the next time someone replies to or mentions them, while the landing page asserts 'You will stop receiving notifications for {title}'; only regular/muted users are actually silenced on the first click, and watching/tracking users must click a second time from yet another unwanted email.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten unsubscribe_link locale makes %{unsubscribe_url} a required interpolation argument for every email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true, but the diff updates only UserNotifications#send_notification_email to pass it — Email::MessageBuilder#html_part (lib/email/message_builder.rb:65) calls I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) with no rescue, so any other add_unsubscribe_link caller raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time and that email is silently never delivered. The diff's own spec (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb) had to be patched to pass unsubscribe_url, proving the new contract is non-obvious; any current or future mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url crashes inside the background send job and users silently stop receiving that mail with no surfaced error and no degradation to the old preferences-only footer.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe dereferences the TopicUser.find_by result with no nil check, so any logged-in user without an existing TopicUser row for that topic gets NoMethodError and a 500 from a public, email-linked GET endpoint. A user who follows a forwarded notification-email link (or any logged-in user who opens /t/<id>/unsubscribe for a topic they never visited, or whose TopicUser rows were destroyed with a deleted topic and not recreated on restore) has no TopicUser row; find_by returns nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, returning the production 500 page instead of creating the row or a 4xx. The same `nil > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` crash fires for existing rows with NULL notification_level (rows written by TopicUser.track_visit! carry no level, which is why the tracking scope COALESCEs it).

[BUG] The unsubscribe toggle demotes a tracking/watching user only to regular instead of muting, so the operation the email and landing page promise (stop receiving notifications for the topic) is only partially applied while being reported as full success. A watching user — the primary recipient of these notification emails — clicks 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and is set to regular, then keeps receiving notification emails whenever someone replies to or mentions them in the topic; the page simultaneously asserts 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>', so the user has no signal that they must click the same link a second time to actually be muted.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe persists the notification-level change via tu.save! directly instead of going through TopicUser.change, skipping the MessageBus {notification_level_change} publish that every other notification-level mutation (TopicUser.change and update_last_read) emits. A user who has the topic open in another browser tab and clicks the email unsubscribe link gets no live update in that tab: the notifications button keeps showing the pre-unsubscribe level (e.g. 'Watching') until a manual refresh, inviting actions based on stale state; the mutation logic is also duplicated outside the model's single entry point, so future changes to level-change side effects miss this path.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe_link locale now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but Email::MessageBuilder supplies no default for it, so building any mail with add_unsubscribe_link: true that does not also pass unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument. Any email type that opts into the unsubscribe footer without supplying the new key — the exact standalone `add_unsubscribe_link: true` invocation the builder's own spec used before this diff, which the diff had to amend to keep passing — dies during mail construction and the send job fails with no email delivered; the option contract of this shared builder changed incompatibly with no guard or fallback (e.g. defaulting unsubscribe_url to user_preferences_url).

[ADVISORY] The topicUnsubscribe model hook returns PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...) with no rejection handler, and the route's actions hash only defines didTransition, so a failed topic fetch is an unhandled promise rejection. When the fetch fails (topic deleted or access revoked between the server render and the client hook, network error, or the preload already consumed on re-entry via browser back), the transition aborts and the user is left on a blank screen with no message — while the server-side unsubscribe mutation has already run, so the user cannot tell whether unsubscribing actually took effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `topicUnsubscribe` route at `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` is declared after the existing `topic.fromParamsNear` route at `/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost` (visible two lines above in the same file), and Ember's router recognizes the earlier-declared route first, so the unsubscribe URL binds nearPost="unsubscribe" to the plain topic route and `topicUnsubscribe` never activates. The unsubscribe confirmation page (route, controller, view, and template — all four new client files) is unreachable dead code; users clicking the email link land on the ordinary topic view with the garbage nearPost flowing into the setupController whose own comment says "closest post is null and this is exploding", and they get no feedback that their notification level was changed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app-route-map.js.es6`, `fromParamsNear` is a nested route with `path: '/:nearPost'` under the topic URL (i.e. it matches `/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost`). The new `topicUnsubscribe` route is added later with `path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe'`, which is also matched by the earlier dynamic `:nearPost` segment (`nearPost = 'unsubscribe'`). Given Ember/router-recognizer’s known “define static routes before dynamic ones” requirement, this ordering makes it likely the `fromParamsNear` route is recognized first and the unsubscribe route/template is unreachable, sending users to the normal topic route with `nearPost='unsubscribe'`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topics#unsubscribe performs a persistent state change (`tu.save!`) on a plain GET with no token, no confirmation, and no guard on the transition, making it the only mutation endpoint in the controller reachable via a side-effecting unauthenticated-token GET. Any third-party page can embed `` — the slug-mismatch branch even 301-redirects to the canonical URL and re-fires — and silently flip the logged-in viewer's notification level (watching→regular, regular→muted) while they never leave the attacker's page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and a `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates persistent state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. Because it is a plain GET and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for `:unsubscribe`, this endpoint is CSRFable via cross-site requests (e.g., an ``). The early 301 redirect on slug mismatch would cause the browser to re-request the canonical URL, at which point the mutation occurs, matching the described silent flip behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The toggle demotes tracking/watching users only to :regular instead of :muted, and regular still emails the user replies, mentions, and quotes for that topic, so the action does not do what the same diff's email copy categorically promises ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic"). A watcher who clicks unsubscribe keeps receiving notification emails for the topic and concludes the unsubscribe is broken (spam complaints follow); they must click the link twice — watching→regular→muted — to get the behavior the email promised in one click.

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new logic explicitly toggles notification level: if the user is above `:regular` (e.g., watching/tracking), it sets them to `:regular`; otherwise it sets them to `:muted` (so a watcher would not be muted in one click). This is diff-verifiable: `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ... else ... muted`.

However, the finding’s stronger claim that `:regular` “still emails the user replies” and that users must click twice to stop receiving topic emails can’t be verified from the diff alone (email-notification semantics for `:regular` aren’t shown here, and the code may already satisfy the intent by removing watching/tracking). The concrete, actionable issue grounded in the diff is the potential mismatch between the email copy (“To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic…”) and the implemented toggle behavior that doesn’t always set `:muted` on first click for watching/tracking users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The action mutates notification_level via direct find/assign/save! instead of the canonical `TopicUser.change` API, silently dropping the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", {notification_level_change: ...})` side effect that every other notification_level write path performs (visible in topic_user.rb in this very diff). A user's other open sessions never receive the notification_level_change message, so the topic notification button shows a stale level until reload; and a second hand-maintained mutation path for the same field has already drifted from the first on both upsert and publish semantics, so the next change to notification semantics must be made twice.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds a new code path that updates `TopicUser#notification_level` via `TopicUser.find_by(...)`, direct assignment, and `tu.save!` without using `TopicUser.change(...)`. In `app/models/topic_user.rb` (also in this diff), `TopicUser.change` is where the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` side effect is implemented for `notification_level` updates. Because the new unsubscribe action bypasses that API, it will not publish the notification_level_change event, so any clients relying on that message (e.g., other open sessions/tabs) won’t be notified of the change until a reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten `unsubscribe_link` string introduces a required `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, and Email::MessageBuilder's html_part (message_builder.rb line 67) passes template_args straight into `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, so any mail built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without the new companion `unsubscribe_url` opt now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action demotes watching/tracking users only to notification_level :regular instead of muting, so a single click on the emailed 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' link does not stop reply/@mention notification emails — and for a tracking user the change is a notification no-op entirely, since tracking and regular have identical email triggers. This contradicts the new copy in `config/locales/server.en.yml` (“To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here”) and `client.en.yml` (“You will stop receiving notifications for …”), because a single click will merely demote higher notification levels to `:regular` rather than ensuring a "stop notifications" state such as `:muted`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe routes are state-mutating GETs whose action is also a toggle (topics_controller.rb:107-111), so every full reload of the confirmation URL re-executes the mutation and flips a regular-level user to muted, and any automated fetcher of the emailed URL (mail scanner, link-preview prefetcher) triggers the state change with no user click at all. It also behaves like a toggle depending on current state (`> regular` -> set to `regular`, else set to `muted`), so hitting the URL can change state repeatedly across visits (e.g., watching->regular on first load, then regular->muted on refresh). Because it is a GET endpoint with no user-confirmed POST/PUT and is linked from emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`), automated fetchers/prefetchers or page reloads can trigger the mutation without an explicit user action. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new unsubscribe action mutates the user's topic notification state via `tu.save!` on a plain unauthenticated GET request carrying no CSRF token and no per-user unsubscribe key, while line 32 explicitly skips the check_xhr filter that gates every other mutating action in this controller, making the mutation cross-site forgeable (Rails authenticity tokens never apply to GET, so Discourse's XHR requirement was the only barrier and it is bypassed for this action). Any attacker-controlled web page embeds `` — the slug-less route added at config/routes.rb:440-441 301-redirects to the canonical URL and browsers follow redirects inside img tags automatically, so only the topic id is needed — and every logged-in user whose browser renders the page has that topic silently demoted (watching/tracking to regular, regular to muted), corrupting their notification preferences with no confirmation and no visible feedback until notifications stop arriving.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route/controller action that changes persisted user state without any CSRF-style protection. `config/routes.rb` introduces `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and the slugged variant, and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (new) toggles `TopicUser.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`. At the same time, the controller explicitly bypasses Discourse’s XHR gate for this action via `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`. Since this is a mutating GET, Rails authenticity tokens won’t apply, making it cross-site forgeable for logged-in users (cookie-authenticated) by embedding the URL (e.g., in an ``).

Any logged-in user who opens the unsubscribe URL for any readable topic they have never interacted with gets an unhandled NoMethodError and a 500 response from the endpoint the emails advertise, instead of a settings change or an error page — the crash is trivially reachable with a handcrafted URL for any public topic.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff adds `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences it via `tu.notification_level` and assigns to `tu.notification_level` before `tu.save!`. The diff includes no nil-handling (e.g., `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`), so if no `topic_users` row exists for that (user, topic) pair, this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` with a triple-stash (unescaped), and that string is built by interpolating the user-controlled topic title (`model.fancyTitle`) into an HTML-bearing I18n message (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 lines 4-6), so topic-title content reaches the DOM with no escaping at the sink. That string is built in the new `topic-unsubscribe` controller by interpolating `model.fancyTitle` into an HTML-bearing I18n string (`stop_notifications: "... {{title}}."`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The email footer added in config/locales/server.en.yml promises 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here', but the action demotes watching/tracking users only to `regular`, a level that still emails direct replies and mentions, so the first click does not actually stop the mail. Users who click the unsubscribe link keep receiving reply/mention notification emails for the topic and conclude the unsubscribe feature is broken — the operator absorbs the spam complaints and support load, and full silence requires a second visit to flip regular to muted.

adjudication.rationale: The new unsubscribe flow promises to “stop receiving notifications about this particular topic” (server.en.yml `unsubscribe_link` and client text `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`), but `TopicsController#unsubscribe` only demotes users with `notification_level > regular` down to `regular` (and only toggles to `muted` on a subsequent visit). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The PR's only test modification (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb is the sole test-shaped file in the diff — I checked all diff paths for spec/test files and found no other) adds unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to the message_with_unsubscribe fixture, but no assertion verifies any of the new per-topic unsubscribe behavior: the assertion consuming the fixture, expect(message_with_unsubscribe.header_args['List-Unsubscribe']).to be_present, checks only that a header key exists and never inspects its value or URL, and the fixture carries no html_override, so Email::MessageBuilder#html_part — the only code path that cooks I18n.t('unsubscribe_link') and substitutes %{unsubscribe_link} (now containing the new %{unsubscribe_url}) into the email body — returns nil immediately and is never executed by this spec. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by with no nil guard, so any logged-in user without a pre-existing TopicUser row for the topic crashes with NoMethodError (undefined method `notification_level' for nil:NilClass) and gets a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page. If `find_by` returns `nil` (no existing `TopicUser` row for that user/topic), this will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500. The diff also shows this URL being embedded into notification emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`), making the nil case plausible for forwarded/guessed links.

A watching or tracking user — the heaviest email recipients this feature targets — clicks the advertised 'stop receiving notifications' link, is set to notification_level regular, and still receives a notification email the next time someone replies to or mentions them, while the landing page asserts 'You will stop receiving notifications for {title}'; only regular/muted users are actually silenced on the first click, and watching/tracking users must click a second time from yet another unwanted email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topics#unsubscribe dereferences the TopicUser.find_by result with no nil check, so any logged-in user without an existing TopicUser row for that topic gets NoMethodError and a 500 from a public, email-linked GET endpoint. A user who follows a forwarded notification-email link (or any logged-in user who opens /t/<id>/unsubscribe for a topic they never visited, or whose TopicUser rows were destroyed with a deleted topic and not recreated on restore) has no TopicUser row; find_by returns nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, returning the production 500 page instead of creating the row or a 4xx. The same `nil > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` crash fires for existing rows with NULL notification_level (rows written by TopicUser.track_visit! carry no level, which is why the tracking scope COALESCEs it).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff introduces `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then assigns `tu.notification_level = ...`, then `tu.save!`) with no nil guard or creation path. If `find_by` returns `nil`, this will raise `NoMethodError`. Additionally, if `tu` exists but `notification_level` is `nil`, `nil > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` will raise. This action is reachable via new GET routes (`/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` etc.) and is also linked from emails via `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, so the crash is a real exposed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe toggle demotes a tracking/watching user only to regular instead of muting, so the operation the email and landing page promise (stop receiving notifications for the topic) is only partially applied while being reported as full success. A watching user — the primary recipient of these notification emails — clicks 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and is set to regular, then keeps receiving notification emails whenever someone replies to or mentions them in the topic; the page simultaneously asserts 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>', so the user has no signal that they must click the same link a second time to actually be muted.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the logic explicitly downgrades any `TopicUser` with `notification_level > :regular` (e.g. tracking/watching) to `:regular`, and only sets `:muted` when the current level is already `<= :regular`: ```rb if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] else tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted] end ``` But both the email copy (`server.en.yml`: “To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here”) and the landing page copy (`client.en.yml` / template: “You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}”) indicate a single action that stops notifications for the topic. The implementation is a toggle requiring potentially two clicks for a watching/tracking user to reach `muted`, which conflicts with the promised outcome and can leave the user still receiving some topic-related notifications while being told they've stopped them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] unsubscribe persists the notification-level change via tu.save! directly instead of going through TopicUser.change, skipping the MessageBus {notification_level_change} publish that every other notification-level mutation (TopicUser.change and update_last_read) emits. A user who has the topic open in another browser tab and clicks the email unsubscribe link gets no live update in that tab: the notifications button keeps showing the pre-unsubscribe level (e.g. 'Watching') until a manual refresh, inviting actions based on stale state; the mutation logic is also duplicated outside the model's single entry point, so future changes to level-change side effects miss this path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the notification level is mutated by fetching a `TopicUser` record and calling `tu.save!` directly, instead of using `TopicUser.change(...)` (diff: `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`). In this diff, `TopicUser.change` is shown to publish a MessageBus event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present (`app/models/topic_user.rb`), but the unsubscribe path will not trigger that publish. This duplicates level-change logic outside the model entry point and may miss side effects (like MessageBus notifications) that other code paths rely on, though the exact UI impact is not directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The unsubscribe_link locale now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but Email::MessageBuilder supplies no default for it, so building any mail with add_unsubscribe_link: true that does not also pass unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument. Any email type that opts into the unsubscribe footer without supplying the new key — the exact standalone `add_unsubscribe_link: true` invocation the builder's own spec used before this diff, which the diff had to amend to keep passing — dies during mail construction and the send job fails with no email delivered; the option contract of this shared builder changed incompatibly with no guard or fallback (e.g. defaulting unsubscribe_url to user_preferences_url).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `Email::MessageBuilder#initialize` does not provide any default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args` (it only seeds `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` and merges opts). In `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part`, when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true it unconditionally calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`, which will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` if `unsubscribe_url` was not supplied by the caller. The accompanying spec had to be amended to pass `unsubscribe_url`, confirming the new required contract; the builder has no guard/fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The topicUnsubscribe model hook returns PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...) with no rejection handler, and the route's actions hash only defines didTransition, so a failed topic fetch is an unhandled promise rejection. When the fetch fails (topic deleted or access revoked between the server render and the client hook, network error, or the preload already consumed on re-entry via browser back), the transition aborts and the user is left on a blank screen with no message — while the server-side unsubscribe mutation has already run, so the user cannot tell whether unsubscribing actually took effect.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` and there is no `catch`/rejection handling or `error` action on this route (only `didTransition`). From the diff alone, it’s verifiable that a rejected `loadTopicView` promise is not handled locally in this route, so the UX/error behavior relies on whatever global Ember/Discourse error handling exists (not shown here). The finding’s specific “blank screen” outcome can’t be proven from the diff, but the underlying concern (missing route-level handling for a failed topic fetch on a page that also triggers a server-side unsubscribe mutation) is diff-grounded.
